title: MATLAB for Engineering
blurb: MATLAB basics for engineering: vectors, matrices, element-wise operations, scripts, functions, plots, conditionals, loops, and switch.
description: A practical MATLAB course for engineering calculations, arrays, functions, control flow, and plotting.

lessons.title: MATLAB environment & command window
objectives: Explain what MATLAB is used for
Enter expressions at the command prompt
lessons.explanation: MATLAB is a numerical-computing environment and programming language for manipulating, analyzing, and visualizing data. Commands and expressions can be entered at the >> prompt in the Command Window.
examples:
r = 8/10; % Compute scalar ratio
u = 0:0.1:10; % Generate sample vector from 0 to 10
z = 5*sin(u); % Scale sine waveform by 5
commonMistakes: Assuming every command must be saved in a script before it can be tested.

lessons.title: Vectors, ranges & transpose
lessons.explanation: Square brackets create vectors. Spaces or commas separate elements in a row, semicolons create a new row, and start: step: end creates regularly spaced values.
examples:
r = [2 4 10]; % Define row vector
y = [2 4 10]'; % Transpose row into column vector
t = 5:0.1:30; % Define time range with 0.1 step
v = 5*r; % Scalar multiply row vector
w = r + v; % Vector addition
u = [r w]; % Horizontal concatenation
commonMistakes: Confusing row separators with element separators.

lessons.title: Matrices & matrix multiplication
lessons.explanation: Matrices use semicolons between rows. Ordinary * performs matrix multiplication, so the inner dimensions must be compatible.
examples:
A = [6 -2; 10 3; 4 7]; % Define 3x2 matrix
B = [9 8; -5 12]; % Define 2x2 matrix
C = A*B; % Matrix multiplication (3x2 * 2x2 = 3x2)
commonMistakes: Using * when element-by-element multiplication is intended.

lessons.title: Element-wise array operations & vectorization
lessons.explanation: Dotted operators apply multiplication, division, or powers element by element. They let one expression operate across an entire vector.
examples:
a = 1:5; % Vector from 1 to 5
b = 3:7; % Vector from 3 to 7
c1 = a.* b; % Element-wise multiplication
c2 = a./ b; % Element-wise division
c3 = a.^ b; % Element-wise exponentiation
x = 0:0.01:1; % Define x domain
y = exp(-x).*sin(x)./sqrt(x.^2 + 1); % Vectorized expression
commonMistakes: Leaving out the dot when the intended operation is element by element.

lessons.title: Scripts & M-files
lessons.explanation: A script file stores a sequence of MATLAB commands for reuse. The example shows running a saved script by typing its filename without the. m extension.
examples:
% prod_abc. m script file
A = [1 4; 2 5]; % Define matrix A
B = [3 6; 1 2]; % Define matrix B
C = A*B; % Compute product C
commonMistakes: Treating a script as if it had function-local inputs and outputs.

lessons.title: Function files & local variables
lessons.explanation: Function files package commands for repeated use. the ARMASM syntax is function [outputs] = function_name(inputs). Function variables are local, and the function name should match the. m filename.
examples:
function y = f2(x) % Function definition with input x
y = 1 - x.*exp(-x); % Local calculation
end % End of function
commonMistakes: Saving the function under a filename that does not match the function name.

lessons.title: Plotting functions & data
objectives: Label axes and add a title
lessons.explanation: plot(x, y) creates an XY graph. xlabel, ylabel, and title describe it; multiple curves can be shown together and legend identifies them.
examples:
x = 0:0.01:2; % Time domain
y = sinh(x); % Hyperbolic sine
z = tanh(x); % Hyperbolic tangent
plot(x, y, x, z,'--'); % Multi-curve plot
xlabel('x'); % X-axis label
ylabel('Hyperbolic sine and tangent'); % Y-axis label
legend('sinh(x)','tanh(x)'); % Curve legends
commonMistakes: Showing multiple curves without labels or a legend.

lessons.title: Relational, logical & conditional statements
lessons.explanation: MATLAB conditionals choose statements from logical expressions. This lesson covers relational operators, logical NOT/AND/OR/xor, and if/elseif/else for piecewise behavior.
examples:
if x >= 5 % Check upper threshold
    y = log(x); % Natural log for high values
elseif x >= 0 % Check positive threshold
    y = sqrt(x); % Square root for non-negative values
else % Negative values
    y = exp(x) - 1; % Exponential for negative values
end % End if structure
commonMistakes: Using = for equality testing instead of ==.

lessons.title: for loops, ranges & implied loops
objectives: Write a for loop using m: s: n
Compare explicit loops with vectorized work
lessons.explanation: The example uses for loop_variable = m: s: n. The step s may be negative and defaults to one when omitted. It also contrasts explicit loops with implied/vectorized array operations.
examples:
x = 0:5:100; % Degree angles
y = cos(x); % Compute cosine vector
for k = 1:21 % Loop through 21 entries
    xv = (k-1)*5; % Current angle
    y2(k) = cos(xv); % Store element
end % End for loop
commonMistakes: Forgetting MATLAB indexing starts at 1 in the explicit-loop example.

lessons.title: while loops & switch structures
objectives: Use while when the iteration count is unknown
lessons.explanation: while is used when repetition stops after a condition changes rather than after a known number of passes. Its controlling value must be initialized and changed. switch provides a readable alternative for discrete cases.
examples:
x = 5; % Initial condition
while x < 25 % Loop while under limit
    disp(x); % Output current value
    x = 2*x - 1; % Update step
end % End while loop

switch angle % Switch on angle variable
    case 45 % Case 45 degrees
        disp('Northeast'); % Display direction
    otherwise % Default case
        disp('Direction Unknown'); % Unknown direction
end % End switch
commonMistakes: Writing a while loop whose controlling value never changes.
